WITH order_avgs AS (
  SELECT AVG(remaincount) as avg_remain
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY COALESCE(ordersmark, 'NULL_ORDER')
),
bench1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(remaincount) as b1
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
),
pass1 AS (
  SELECT oa.avg_remain
  FROM order_avgs oa
  WHERE oa.avg_remain > (SELECT b1 FROM bench1)
),
bench2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_remain) as b2
  FROM pass1
),
pass2 AS (
  SELECT p1.avg_remain
  FROM pass1 p1
  WHERE p1.avg_remain > (SELECT b2 FROM bench2)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(p2.avg_remain),
  AVG(p2.avg_remain - (SELECT b1 FROM bench1)),
  AVG(p2.avg_remain - (SELECT b2 FROM bench2))
FROM pass2 p2

assumptions.assumption: NULL remaincount values are ignored when calculating per-order averages and the first benchmark (standard SQL AVG behavior excludes NULLs).
NULL ordersmark values are grouped together as a single 'order' rather than excluded entirely.
